hints: Find the midpoint $M$ of base $BC$ by averaging coordinates of $B(-2, 1)$ and $C(6, 1)$.
Use the distance formula between vertex $A(2, 7)$ and midpoint $M(2, 1)$ to find $AM = 7 - 1 = 6$.
walkthrough:
The altitude of this isosceles triangle meets the midpoint of its base.
Calculate the midpoint $M$ of base $BC$:
$$M = \left(\dfrac{-2 + 6}{2}, \dfrac{1 + 1}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{4}{2}, \dfrac{2}{2}\right) = (2, 1)$$

Calculate the length of the altitude $AM$:
$$AM = \sqrt{(2 - 2)^2 + (7 - 1)^2} = \sqrt{0^2 + 6^2} = 6$$
